events.subtitle: BODY&SOUL Final Groove daytime quartet
events.category: Japanese jazz masters / vocal-piano quartet / historic-club final month
events.factual_description: BODY&SOUL lists Kimiko Ito with Tsuyoshi Yamamoto, Daiki Yasukagawa and Kazuhiro Ebisawa on Sunday, September 6, 2026. Doors are at 14:00, with sets at 15:00 and 16:30. The club has announced that its 52-year run ends in September 2026 and identifies July 1 through September 26 as its Final Groove period.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the exact meeting, not Yamamoto's name alone: Ito's mature vocal phrasing sits against Yamamoto's rhythmic piano language, with Daiki Yasukagawa and Kazuhiro Ebisawa completing a serious quartet, and it happens inside the closing month of a Tokyo club with more than five decades of history. That gives an otherwise plausible jazz-vocal date a concrete Listening Notes thread and a finite live setting.
en.trip_verdict: If September 6 overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for one of the afternoon sets and let Shibuya organize the outing. The closing-month context makes it worth prioritizing while there, but it is not enough by itself to justify a dedicated Japan trip.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho es el encuentro exacto, no el nombre de Yamamoto por sí solo: el fraseo vocal maduro de Ito se cruza con el lenguaje rítmico del piano de Yamamoto, con Daiki Yasukagawa y Kazuhiro Ebisawa completando un cuarteto serio, y todo ocurre durante el último mes de un club de Tokio con más de cinco décadas de historia. Eso convierte una fecha de jazz vocal que podría ser recurrente en un hilo concreto de Listening Notes con un contexto en vivo finito.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 6 de septiembre coincide con Tokio, le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets de la tarde y armaría la salida alrededor de Shibuya. El contexto del último mes hace que valga la pena priorizarla estando allá, pero por sí solo no justifica un viaje dedicado a Japón.

en.why_it_matters: The centennial framing has substance because both leaders carry a direct musical relationship to the legacies being examined: Ravi Coltrane approaches his father's language from inside his own mature voice, while Blanchard has spent decades extending the trumpet vocabulary that Miles helped transform. With Altura, Oren, Ginyard and Petinaud, the stated goal is reimagining rather than repertory imitation, which makes the performance a live argument about what those innovations still permit now.
en.trip_verdict: This is local enough to make room for directly: build the North Bethesda evening around the 8:00 PM set rather than treating it as corridor travel. The collaboration appears in multiple 2026 cities, so the reason to go is the quality and local opportunity, not a claim that this exact project exists only once.

events.artist: New Jersey Symphony with Christian McBride
events.subtitle: Rachmaninoff’s Symphonic Dances — George Duke’s Dark Wood / Christian McBride’s Fried Bacon

venue.name: Prudential Hall, New Jersey Performing Arts Center

events.category: Jazz-classical crossover / double-bass concerto / first New Jersey Symphony collaboration
events.factual_description: New Jersey Symphony performs Rachmaninoff’s Symphonic Dances at NJPAC in Newark on November 19, 2026 at 1:30 PM. Eric Jacobsen conducts, with Christian McBride on double bass and Chris Komer on horn. The program includes George Duke’s Dark Wood: Bass Concerto for Christian McBride, McBride’s orchestral work Fried Bacon, Debussy’s Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun and Rachmaninoff’s Symphonic Dances. New Jersey Symphony states that McBride solos with the orchestra for the first time; the November 19 and 22 Newark performances are part of the TD James Moody Jazz Festival.

enrichment.note: New Jersey Symphony verifies the exact Newark date/time, program, personnel, first-orchestra collaboration and authorized ticketing destination. No exact Apple Music destination is supplied without verification.

sources.note: Primary event page verifies all three program dates, the two Newark performances, full announced personnel, program, TD James Moody Jazz Festival context and McBride's first solo appearance with the orchestra.
Authorized New Jersey Symphony ticketing destination listing the November 19 Newark performance.

provenance.note: Date, time, venue, personnel, program, first New Jersey Symphony collaboration and authorized ticketing were verified from New Jersey Symphony. Repository-wide searches for this Christian McBride / New Jersey Symphony Newark performance on 2026-11-19 returned no existing RADAR match before publication.

en.why_it_matters: The double bass is not a crossover ornament here; it is the structural reason the program belongs in RADAR. George Duke wrote Dark Wood for McBride's specific combination of groove and virtuosity, and Fried Bacon carries McBride's own writing into the orchestral frame. Hearing that material in his first solo appearance with the New Jersey Symphony puts a major improvising bassist in dialogue with symphonic mass and color rather than merely dropping a jazz guest into a pops program.
en.trip_verdict: The 1:30 PM Thursday matinee can work as the musical anchor of a deliberate Newark day if the corridor trip is already feasible; pair it with an evening reason in Newark or New York rather than making the train ride for a short turnaround.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el contrabajo no funciona como adorno de crossover; es la razón estructural por la que el programa pertenece al RADAR. George Duke escribió Dark Wood para la combinación específica de groove y virtuosismo de McBride, y Fried Bacon lleva la propia escritura de McBride al marco orquestal. Escuchar ese material en su primera aparición como solista con la New Jersey Symphony pone a un gran bajista improvisador en diálogo con la masa y el color sinfónicos, en vez de insertar a un invitado de jazz en un programa de pops.
es.trip_verdict: La matiné del jueves a la 1:30 PM puede funcionar como ancla musical de un día deliberado en Newark si el viaje por el corredor ya es viable; la combinaría con otra razón nocturna en Newark o Nueva York en vez de hacer ida y vuelta rápida sólo por el concierto.
